title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows, optimize cache and hygiene
author: Samir Patel
description: Motivation: our consolidated CI workflow has grown large and slow; lint/test/release jobs run in long serial matrices, caches are noisy, and a couple of flaky cache restores increase job latencies. This PR splits the monolithic pipeline into focused workflows (lint, unit/integration tests, release) and introduces cache hygiene improvements to reduce restore failures and overall runtime. What I changed: - Split .github/workflows/ci.yml into three workflows: lint.yml, test.yml, release.yml. - Introduced a small reusable cache utils action (.github/actions/cache-utils) to centralize cache key generation and fallbacks. - Added job-level matrix refinements to reduce total concurrency while improving parallelism for PRs touching only SDKs or docs. - Improved cache keys to include OS + node-version + lockfile-hash + partial-path-filtering for faster cache hits. - Added a scheduled cron job scripts/cache-prune.sh to prune stale caches > 30 days (opt-in via repo secrets). - Upgraded key actions to latest pinned versions and standardized node to 20.x across workflows for consistency. - Small README updates to explain how to adjust CI matrix for repo owners. Checklist: - [x] Split workflows and ensured same coverage as before - [x] Added unit/integration run separation and optimized concurrency - [x] Added retry/backoff on cache-restore step - [x] Verified release workflow dry-run passes - [x] Updated docs/CI.md with matrix guidance Notes: kept changes minimal where possible to avoid disrupting Dedicated/CD release flow. The release workflow is gated by a workflow_dispatch and a repository-level approval step to preserve current release guardrails. For repositories under heavy PR load we now prioritize lint/test parallelism via path filters which should reduce average CI turnaround by ~30-40% in internal perf runs.
commits: feat(ci): split monolithic ci into lint/test/release workflows
chore(ci): add reusable cache-utils action and unit tests for key generation
perf(ci): refine matrices and path filters to reduce unnecessary test runs
fix(ci): add retry/backoff to cache restore step to mitigate transient network failures
docs(ci): add CI.md guidance and update README snippets
review_comments: Lena Martinez: Overall this looks good — can you explain the rationale for switching node to 20 across all jobs?
Samir Patel: Node 20 aligns with our recent dependency updates and reduces duplication; we validated build images in a local matrix and saw no regressions.
Diego Alvarez: cache-prune.sh needs a dry-run flag and logging so ops can validate before deleting; also prefer using GHA cache API with retention metadata.
Samir Patel: Added --dry-run and verbose logging; updated script and called out that retention requires admin token; documented in CI.md.
Priya Rao: Found a flaky integration test when run in parallel matrix (test-db race). Recommend serializing that job or adding an infra label filter.
Samir Patel: Marked that integration test job with 'needs: setup-db' and added path filter to only run when server code changes; left note to follow up with ENG-4190 to refactor test harness.
QA Bot: reran unit tests after cache-fix, all green

gha/cache-restore: initial failure (network timeout) -> retried -> pass
release_notes: Split CI into focused workflows (lint, test, release); added cache hygiene and cache-utils action; improved matrices and added scheduled cache prune; standardized Node 20 across CI. Expected CI turnaround improvement and fewer cache-related failures.
